question: Should the repair lane adopt this stricter fail-closed mutation contract now, accepting that legacy or drifted operations will block or requeue rather than preserve the previous continuation behavior?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well covered, but only a maintainer can accept the operational tradeoff between stronger authorization integrity and temporary repair-lane interruption during stale state, API races, or legacy authorization data.

options.title: Approve strict rollout after canary
options.body: Accept fail-closed blocking as the permanent contract and merge after one exact-current-head controlled canary confirms retry and publication behavior.

options.title: Stage compatibility migration
options.body: Add a bounded migration or rollout phase for legacy authorization state before enforcing the strict contract everywhere.

options.title: Pause the rollout
options.body: Keep the PR open until maintainers are comfortable that expected repair throughput and recovery behavior justify the stricter boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve strict rollout after canary
recommendation.body: Accept fail-closed blocking as the permanent contract and merge after one exact-current-head controlled canary confirms retry and publication behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the merged prerequisite and the current repair mutation-safety implementation, making them the best available routing candidate for the rollout decision.
